articles.headline: Trump says he’d ‘love’ to have Sen. John Fetterman as a Republican amid growing speculation
keyFacts: Donald Trump said he would welcome Democratic Senator John Fetterman into the Republican Party.
A reporter questioned Trump after Fetterman repeatedly broke with Democrats during the current session of Congress.
Trump claimed it would be hard for Fetterman to win the Democratic nomination and praised his common sense.
body: Trump says he’d ‘love’ to have Sen. John Fetterman as a Republican amid growing speculation
By
Michael Sinkewicz, Fox News
Published Oct. 10, 2026, 10:37 p.m. PT
See more of our coverage in your search results.
President Donald Trump praised Sen. John Fetterman, D-Pa., as a “great guy” on Saturday, saying he would welcome the Pennsylvania Democrat into the Republican Party.

Trump was asked by a reporter after stepping off Air Force One at Joint Base Andrews whether he had spoken to Fetterman — who has repeatedly broken with Democrats during the current session of Congress — about becoming a Republican and whether he would welcome such a switch.
“I’d love to see it. I think he’s great,” Trump responded.
“It’s going to be hard for him to get the nomination as a Democrat, but I’d love to have him as a Republican,” he continued.
Trump described Fetterman as a “great guy” with “magnificent parents,” whom he said he had spoken with previously.
“He’s a very solid person,” Trump added. “He’s smart and all that, but he’s got great common sense.”

articles.headline: Dodgers’ Dave Roberts sends message to Shohei Ohtani before NLCS amid slump
keyFacts: Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts eased expectations for Shohei Ohtani ahead of the NLCS due to his recent batting slump.
Ohtani struggled offensively in the NL Division Series against the Atlanta Braves after missing most of September with various injuries.
Roberts stated that any positive contribution, such as drawing a walk or getting on base, is sufficient for the team.
body: Brett Davis-Imagn Images. Dodgers’ Dave Roberts sends message to Shohei Ohtani before NLCS amid slump appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here .

Shohei Ohtani has not looked like himself this October, and the Los Angeles Dodgers are not asking him to carry the load right away. Ahead of Game 1 of the National League Championship Series against the Milwaukee Brewers , manager Dave Roberts lowered the bar for his superstar.

“For tomorrow it’s just get on base, take good at-bats, and we’ll deal with whatever,” Roberts said. “Honestly, it’s the same message for everyone. Shohei is known for his slug, but when you’re facing Jacob (Misiorowski), it’s just you’ve got to take good at-bats.”
Roberts made it clear that any positive contribution will do.
Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)
“If you run into a homer, great. But if you can earn a walk, fantastic,” Roberts said. “Production is just doing anything positive for the club, and we need all guys to do their part.”

Ohtani went just 2-for-13 with four strikeouts and two walks in the NL Division Series against the Atlanta Braves. Roberts even dropped him to fifth in the batting order for Game 3 against left-hander Chris Sale, a move he said was specific to that matchup.
“He’s scuffling right now, but I really believe that he’s going to come to life at some point,” Roberts said during that series.
The slump comes after Ohtani missed most of September with various injuries , giving him only five tune-up games in the final week of the regular season before the playoffs began.
The Dodgers survived anyway. They eliminated Atlanta with a 4-1 win in Game 4 on Wednesday, even as Ohtani, Mookie Betts, Freddie Freeman and Will Smith combined to go 0-for-15 in the clincher.

Misiorowski has been one of the toughest pitchers the Dodgers have faced , posting a 1.59 ERA with 27 strikeouts and just three walks over 17 innings against them in two regular-season starts and one relief appearance in last year’s NLCS.
L os Angeles will counter with Tarik Skubal on the mound in Milwaukee, with Yoshinobu Yamamoto lined up for Game 2 on Monday.

Roberts’ approach takes some pressure off his star. If Ohtani can simply grind out at-bats against one of the league’s most overpowering arms, the Dodgers will gladly take it as they chase a third straight World Series title.

articles.headline: Colts rule out 5 players for Week 5 vs. Steelers, including key defenders
keyFacts: The Indianapolis Colts ruled out five players for their Week 5 game against the Pittsburgh Steelers.
The injured players include linebackers, wide receivers, a defensive end, and a tight end.
The players were sidelined due to injuries affecting their ribs, ankles, hamstrings, thumbs, and knees.
body: The Pittsburgh Steelers ' Week 5 opponent, the Indianapolis Colts , have ruled out several players for Sunday's matchup.

Courtesy of the final Week 5 injury report, the Colts ruled out five players for their game against the Steelers : linebacker Jaylon Carlies, wide receiver Ashton Dulin, defensive end Arden Key, tight end Will Mallory, and wide receiver Darius Slayton.

After missing the first 11 games of the 2025 season, Carlies has had a concerning injury history. He's appeared in the first four games for Indianapolis but suffered a rib injury in the Colts' Week 4 win that ultimately led to him getting ruled out in Week 5.

Dulin previously suffered an ankle injury in Week 1 and missed the team's next two games. Despite returning in Week 4, Dulin suffered a hamstring injury, which ultimately led to him being sidelined for Sunday's game against the Steelers.

Key has appeared in every game so far for Indianapolis this season but suffered a hamstring injury in the team's Week 4 win over the Washington Commanders . He was unable to log a single practice this week and was ruled out on Friday.

Mallory, listed as the fourth-string tight end on the Colts' depth chart, put together a strong performance in the team's preseason opener before suffering a thumb sprain at training camp practice on August 20. He was placed on injured reserve on August 31 and returned to Week 5 practice on Wednesday as a full participant, but the Colts decided to hold him out for Sunday's game against the Steelers.

Slayton, who spent his first seven years with the New York Giants and has yet to make his debut with the Colts, was originally designated as questionable with a knee injury for Week 5 before the team downgraded him to out on Saturday.

articles.headline: India court orders release of 'Cockroach' movement leaders
keyFacts: A Delhi court ordered the release of three Cockroach Janta Party leaders after nearly 24 hours in detention, the movement said.
The youth-led movement organized protests calling for the resignation of India's election chief over alleged manipulation of voter lists.
The Cockroach Janta Party called for a fresh protest march to New Delhi's Jantar Mantar on Sunday.
body: What you need to know
Here are the latest developments from India on Sunday, October 11:
- The CJP's Abhijeet Dipke, Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das ordered released after nearly 24 hours of detention
- Indian media reports cite Delhi Police officials as saying thousands of detained protesters were released
- The CJP called for a fresh protest on Sunday
Tired of missing our real-time updates? Click here to add us as a Preferred Source on Google. Then tap the "Star" or "Preferred" to keep DW News at the top of your feed.
'Cockroach' leaders ordered released from detention, party says
An executive court in Delhi has ordered the release of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke and other leaders Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka, the youth-led movement said on Sunday.
The three were detained ahead of a large protest in Dehli on Saturday and appeared in court earlier on Sunday after being in detention for nearly 24 hours.
Earlier, the CJP had alleged the leaders were being detained at an undisclosed location and did not have access to their lawyers.
On Saturday evening, the CJP issued a fresh call for a march to New Delhi's Jantar Mantar on Sunday.
"We're not backing down! We will march to Jantar Mantar again tomorrow," Ajinkya Shinde, the CJP's interim protest leader, said at a press conference.
The exact number of demonstrators detained during the protest could not be immediately verified.
Shinde told reporters that over 15,000 people, including students, had been detained across India.
The Hindu newspaper, citing Delhi Police sources, reported that 2,500 demonstrators were detained in Delhi on top of 1,000 people picked up in overnight preventive measures ahead of the protest.
Indian media reports cite Delhi Police as saying that all detainees had been released later on Saturday.
Welcome to our coverage
This is Dharvi Vaid Dhulia from DW's Studio in New Delhi, bringing you the Sunday edition of the India news blog.
We are continuing our coverage of the intensifying election protests in India over alleged manipulation of voter lists.
Here's a quick recap of what went down on Saturday:

Dramatic scenes unfolded in the streets of the capital of the world's largest democracy on Saturday as authorities tried to thwart a protest called by the "Cockroach" movement calling for the resignation of India's election chief.

Thousands of youth protesters were detained and hauled away in buses as parts of Delhi were locked down with a mammoth deployment of police and paramilitary personnel, who essentially outnumbered the demonstrators.
Mobile internet services were suspended in central Delhi in a rare move for the key power district, while dozens of metro stations were closed.

Police cited violation of a ban on the protest as basis for the mass detentions. The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) and student organizations supporting the demonstration maintain that they did not need permission, citing protesting as a fundamental right.
The three main faces of the CJP — Founder Abhijeet Dipke, Co-conveners Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka — were detained onboard a plane as soon as they landed in New Delhi for the protest.

Meanwhile, four former chief ministers of Indian states were also briefly detained during the protest, amid the opposition parties stepping up their calls for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
Stay tuned as we bring you more.

articles.headline: Gary Larson's 10 Greatest 'Far Side' Comics, Ranked
keyFacts: Polygon published a ranked list of the 10 greatest comic strips from Gary Larson's The Far Side.
The author argues that greatness in The Far Side should be measured by the cleverness and effectiveness of each daily joke.
The top-ranked comic features dinosaurs smoking cigarettes, combining the author's love of dark humor and dinosaur themes.
body: What, exactly, is the measure of greatness when it comes to comic strips? The daily newspaper comic is a very limiting art form, with only a few panels — sometimes just one panel — to make a joke. Because of its brevity, it's easy to trivialize the medium as simply the “funny papers,” a daily, disposable art form designed to pick you up after reading the actual news.

Yet, we’ve seen comic strips do so much more than that. Characters like Snoopy and Garfield have become part of the fabric of our culture. Comic strips are capable of greatness. And since greatness is possible, what, then, makes a comic strip great?

The first instinct is to go for something “deep.” Comic strips like Peanuts and Calvin and Hobbes occasionally ventured outside of comedy to examine the world and say something thoughtful about it. But that’s not the case for other comic strips that don’t go deep. For Garfield, I’d argue greatness would come down to a really clever, relatable gag. For something like Prince Valiant, which specialized in highly detailed, picturesque images, I imagine greatness would relate to visual appeal.
So what would the measure of greatness be for Gary Larson’s The Far Side?

The Far Side didn’t do deep and life-affirming stuff. Nor was Larson's comic beautiful in any conventional sense, as his characters were often grotesque to enhance the comedy. It's tempting to associate greatness with the comic strips that made the biggest impact, like the Stegosaurus strip that resulted in a new name for a dinosaur bone, but Larson’s work never set out to end up in science books.

I’d argue that what Gary Larson was doing with The Far Side was trying to make the funniest joke each day. That's why he didn't use recurring characters — it wasn't about characters so much as the joke. Thus I’d argue, for The Far Side, greatness should be measured by the effectiveness and cleverness of the joke. Making us laugh was the purpose of The Far Side, so I can’t think of a better means by which to measure them.
So here are 10 Far Side comics that I think are Larson's best, not because they made headlines or they said something profound about life, but because they're just really clever and funny.
10 Find Peter

One of the highlights of Larson’s work was just how much he trusted his audience. Sometimes the punchlines were broad and dumb — in the best way — and sometimes his comics were like a comedic scavenger hunt. This is a great example of a joke that only pays off when you figure out which cubicle you’re supposed to look in.
9 A deconstructionist masterpiece

Gary Larson didn’t do it often, but sometimes he used The Far Side to break the fourth wall with the reader — he would use a comic panel to deconstruct the art of comic strips. For example, this comic is about “sketchy” looking characters, so it features characters that are especially crudely drawn. It's really clever, but you’ve got to pay fairly close attention to get it.
8 And the complete opposite kind of masterpiece

But a Far Side didn’t require subtlety to be great. For this one, it’s funny because of the overkill. It’s obvious the man was killed with a bowling pin, and the joke is that it's still a mystery for these idiot cops, despite the fact they are surrounded by hundreds of bowling pins.
7 A clever twist

Oftentimes, The Far Side would find a way to put a brand new spin on something very old. The Peter Pan example up top is a good one, but I’d argue this one about Pinocchio is even funnier. Pinocchio's whole thing is that he wants to be a real boy, so what’s a situation where he suddenly wouldn’t want that?
6 More deconstruction

Here’s another example of Larson subverting the medium, even if it’s not exactly his own medium. Along with their daily comic strips, newspapers often featured activity panels, like “spot the differences” and “hidden images.” In this Far Side, Larson is mocking hidden images comics by showing a bunch of badly hidden appliances in a forest. The punchline is the best part, as it says there are 127 appliances here, which there obviously aren’t.
5 Find the punchline

This is another great example of a scavenger hunt for the punchline. The first thing your eye sees is the giant fly woman, then you go to the woman the artist is painting. Finally, you see what’s on the artist’s glasses.
4 Reconstruct the punchline
This comic takes the “find the punchline” thing even further. Here, it takes a few seconds before you realize that the joke is that there was a window washer, before the woman opened the window.
3 Snakes

While Larson never really went deep on the meaning of existence, he sometimes tackled the silliness of it all in really funny ways. The idea that God made snakes the same way a kid does with Play-Doh is such a clever idea that sort of trivializes all of existence.
2 Love triangle
Like the bowling pin comic, this joke's cleverness comes from the characters' lack of cleverness.
1 Smoking dinosaurs

This is a really famous Far Side, but not because it changed dinosaur history. It’s beloved because it shows off a lot of wonderful Larson traits all in one place. Larson loved comics with dinosaurs. He also loved to make really dark, morbid jokes. On its surface, the image of dinosaurs smoking cigarettes is hilariously lowbrow, but the idea that they went extinct from smoking is incredibly clever. That’s why this is Larson’s best-ever Far Side, because it’s a whole lot of Larson all in one little rectangle.

articles.headline: Dynasty Warriors 3: Complete Edition Remastered review: Welcome (back) to China
keyFacts: TechRadar reported that Dynasty Warriors 3: Complete Edition Remastered releases on October 1, 2026, for PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S, and Nintendo Switch 2.
The reviewer stated that the remaster preserves the original game while adding optional modern quality-of-life features, a visual facelift, and content from the Xtreme Legends expansion.
The reviewer noted that players complete bite-sized campaigns in Musou Mode to unlock characters, weapons, and rare items across four main factions.
body: TechRadar Verdict

Dynasty Warriors 3: Complete Edition Remastered is one of the most thoughtful and forward-thinking remasters I’ve played in some time. The original game, warts and all, is intact, but some light quality-of-life touches freshen up the experience without detracting from its intended feel.
Reasons to buy
- + Tons of characters to unlock
- + Replayability through higher difficulties and hidden objectives
- + New gameplay features polish up the experience
- + Corny dialogue and that excellent soundtrack are fully intact
- + Satisfyingly challenging
Reasons to avoid
- - Some maps are a slog to get around
- - Newcomers might not gel with enemy aggression
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.

Revisiting one of Omega Force’s most beloved works via Dynasty Warriors 3: Complete Edition Remastered has been interesting. I got into the series quite late, so I’ve never had the same reverence for the earlier games that many other fans do. I’m happy to say that has changed with this remastered version.
Platform reviewed: PC
Available on: PS5, Xbox Series X|S, Nintendo Switch 2, PC
Release date: October 1, 2026

This is a very different game compared to modern entries like Dynasty Warriors Origins or Hyrule Warriors: Age of Imprisonment. Objectives are straightforward, battles (for the most part) tend not to last as long, and your KO count per battle is much lower than the thousands you rack up in newer installments.

Satisfaction lies elsewhere in Dynasty Warriors 3: Complete Edition Remastered. It trades bombastic theatrics and ‘rule of cool’ battlefield domination for a more grounded approach. Instead of tearing across battlegrounds like a Category 5 hurricane, you’ll need to pick your fights more carefully and move with your army. Even basic peons are far more aggressive in this game, so ditching your allies isn’t exactly the wisest decision.

There are some cool quality-of-life additions, such as being able to counter enemy Strong and Special attacks with your own. A handy checkpoint feature lets you rewind the battle to key moments if you die, and there’s an honest-to-goodness dodge button that helps even the odds and can even be followed up with a counter if timed correctly. Alternatively, you can set the entire game to a ‘Classic’ mode, ditching all of this in favor of the original gameplay experience.

It’s an incredibly thoughtful remaster in that regard, offering options for newcomers, purists, and everyone in between. The visual facelift is nice, but not overbearing. Plus, additional content from the Xtreme Legends expansion is included here, too, making Dynasty Warriors 3: Complete Edition Remastered an extremely beefy package for its relatively budget price tag.
Same as it ever was?

Dynasty Warriors 3: Complete Edition Remastered, as ever, presents a loose interpretation of Luo Guanzhong’s Romance of the Three Kingdoms. Which in itself is a romanticization of this turbulent wartorn era of Ancient China.

As an earlier entry, Dynasty Warriors 3 pretty much gives you the highlights rather than delving deep into character drama or motivations. It’s quite refreshingly simple, though individual playable officers do get their own cutscenes, endings, and the like.

You’ll spend the majority of your time in Musou Mode — effectively the game’s campaign. You will then choose an officer from one of four factions: Wei, Wu, Shu, or Other. The latter of which featuring officers with no set affiliation like Lu Bu, Dong Zhuo, and Diaochan.

Each officer has their own bespoke Musou Mode route, though some are longer than others. Even so, your goal on each map typically boils down to defeating a key enemy officer, while ticking off smaller objectives to boost your side’s morale or rob the enemy of powerful weaponry.

That might sound repetitive, and it can be if played over longer sessions. However, I think Dynasty Warriors 3: Complete Edition Remastered is tailored to shorter bursts of play, and the bite-sized Musou Mode campaigns for each officer support that. Playing through a campaign will bolster that officer’s stats, as well as earn them new weapons and equippable items — the latter of which can be shared between all officers.

Part of the beauty of Dynasty Warriors 3: Complete Edition Remastered is that it feels like a snowball of unlockables. You’ll routinely be bagging new playable officers, more powerful weapons, and potent rare items should you meet their conditions during a stage.

Some stages can also grant you an officer’s fourth or fifth weapon. These are extremely strong, but are typically gated behind higher difficulties and some rather stringent objectives so be sure to bring upgraded officers and plenty of patience for these.
Old and new

One of my favorite things about Dynasty Warriors 3: Complete Edition Remastered is that it has options for basically everyone. You can play the entire game in either modern or classic modes. Classic is just that: Dynasty Warriors 3 as it played on the PlayStation 2, for the most part. No fancy extras. Does it feel a bit dated? Yes absolutely, but I’m happy it’s here as an option for purists.

The more modern take applies a bunch of quality-of-life changes and gameplay additions. As mentioned at the top, these include Strong and Special attack counters, a dodge, and a quick mount option for your horse. It helps the game feel a lot more fluid, in my opinion.

Was I still getting juggled to death by lowly peons for daring to take on an officer on my lonesome? Yep. More than a few times. But ultimately I did appreciate the more humbling experience here when I’m so used to treating enemy armies like mowing the lawn in more modern Musou games.

Dynasty Warriors 3: Complete Edition Remastered is a reminder of how cool unlockable content used to be in this era of gaming. You’ll have to put the work in to unlock most characters as well as their signature weapons. It’s the kind of stuff that’ll keep you busy for potentially tens of hours without feeling overly tedious.

What’s nice is that if you’re somewhere in the middle — say, wanting a hybrid modern/classic experience — Dynasty Warriors 3: Complete Edition Remastered supports that. Quality-of-life additions can be toggled individually in the options menu, allowing for a widely customizable experience.

Additions aside, Omega Force has elected to keep the original game’s amazing soundtrack and cheeseball dialogue fully intact. I love this because there are some truly hilarious line deliveries across cutscenes, and the overt mispronunciation of officer names just adds to the charm of it all. Battles have been spiced up with combat lines from later entries like Dynasty Warriors 8, though, which is a nice touch.
Should I play Dynasty Warriors 3: Complete Edition Remastered?
Play it if…
You’re a newer Musou fan

If you’ve only recently gotten into Omega Force’s Warriors franchise, I implore you to give this one a go. It’s a great change of pace from more modern entries and very much bears a ‘substance over style’ approach.
You love unlockables
There are boatloads of officers and weapons to unlock, and most play rather differently from one another.
Don't play it if...
You’re not keen on repetition

There isn’t really any grinding to be done here, but replaying Musou Mode with many different officers can grow tiresome. Oh, and as a bonus pro tip: you only have to do a particularly aggravating objective during the Nanman campaign mission once, but my word is it a slog that first time.
Accessibility features

There aren't any dedicated accessibility toggles in Dynasty Warriors 3: Complete Edition Remastered such as subtitles or colorblind modes. However, individual game settings can be toggled based on preferences. These include target-facing assists, dodging, power guards, and strong attack counters.
How I reviewed Dynasty Warriors 3: Complete Edition Remastered

I played Dynasty Warriors 3: Complete Edition Remastered for 15 hours on PC via Steam for this review. Being a remaster of an older title, my Nvidia GeForce RTX 5060 was more than enough to run the game on maximum settings with zero hitches or issues.
My gamepad of choice was the Valve Steam Controller (2026), and I often hooked up my RIG 900 Max HS gaming headset to enjoy the game's banging soundtrack and corny dialogue sequences.
The majority of my playtime was spent in the main Musou Mode, unlocking characters, weapons, and optional rare items. Though I did delve into the Free and Challenge modes for a change of pace, too.

Particularly passionate about high-quality third-party controllers and headsets, Rhys strives to provide easy-to-read, informative coverage on gaming hardware of all kinds. As for the games themselves, Rhys is especially keen on fighting and racing games, as well as soulslikes and RPGs.

articles.headline: Justice Department investigating TV networks that briefly suspended Trump press pool coverage
keyFacts: The Justice Department is investigating whether major television networks broke antitrust laws by temporarily suspending White House pool coverage.
A Justice Department spokesperson stated that the inquiry examines whether the networks' group boycott violated the Sherman Act.
The networks suspended their coverage after the White House revoked credentials for journalists from CNN, MSNOW, and Politico.
body: The Justice Department is investigating whether the major TV networks violated antitrust law last month when they briefly suspended their pool coverage of President Donald Trump after he blocked multiple news outlets from fully accessing White House grounds.

ABC, CBS, CNN, NBC, and Fox News were told on Friday to provide “communications and materials” related to the White House TV press pool, according to the New York Times , in an escalation against legacy media companies with which Trump has long feuded.

The White House announced it had rescinded the credentials of journalists working for CNN , MSNOW , and Politico on Sept. 18, largely citing national security concerns over the outlets’ reporting on the conflict in Iran. The five networks that make up the TV press pool, which documents the president’s daily travels and distributes video footage, then announced they would withhold their coverage of Trump’s summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping in an act of solidarity. Trump would later lament the moment was “made for Television” but the “Fake News” didn’t want to cover it.

“Members of the television press pool have boycotted covering White House events,” Justice Department spokesperson Emily Covington said Saturday in a statement. “Group boycotts among commercial competitors can violate the Sherman Act. The Antitrust Division is simply investigating to determine whether these news organizations have violated the antitrust laws.” The Sherman Act is a landmark federal law passed in 1890 that seeks to ensure free competition and prohibit monopolistic business activity.

“The public has a vital interest in receiving accurate, independent information about its government,” the five networks said in a group statement when explaining their decision. “No administration should reject a news organization because it objects to its reporting.”
DOJ INVESTIGATING CASSIDY HUTCHINSON OVER HOUSE JAN. 6 COMMITTEE TESTIMONY

The three newspapers’ credentials were restored after Trump-appointed U.S. District Judge Timothy Kelly granted a temporary restraining order against the ban following a joint lawsuit. The Trump administration has continued to bar CNN and Politico from the Oval Office and Air Force One.

Trump has long cast his political rise as a battle against the legacy media companies that he believes cover him unfairly. His rallying cry against the “Fake News” became a defining feature of his initial 2016 presidential campaign, helping him garner support among voters who distrust established institutions.

articles.headline: US opens antitrust probe into TV networks halting Trump coverage
keyFacts: The US Department of Justice opened an antitrust probe into television networks that halted coverage of President Donald Trump.
ABC, CBS, CNN, NBC, and Fox News boycotted coverage after the administration barred three news organizations from the White House.
The Justice Department is investigating whether the networks' group boycott violated federal antitrust laws, a spokesperson said.
body: The United States Department of Justice has opened an investigation into television networks’ decision to halt coverage of President Donald Trump last month.

A spokesperson said on Saturday that the department was investigating whether the networks violated federal antitrust laws by their boycott, which followed a White House decision to pull the credentials of reporters from three news organisations, including CNN.
The networks under investigation are ABC, CBS, CNN, NBC and Fox News, said Emily Convington, the Justice Department spokesperson.
“Group boycotts among commercial competitors can violate the Sherman Act,” she said of the antitrust legislation.
“The Antitrust Division is simply investigating to determine whether these news organizations have violated the antitrust laws.”

The investigation is the latest in a series of clashes between the Trump administration and major news organisations. Trump has repeatedly called the mainstream media “fake news” and frequently clashes with reporters during encounters with the press.
The action also puts legal and potentially financial pressure on the media to continue coverage of the president even when they disagree with how the White House handles them.
The networks did not immediately comment on the announcement.

The Justice Department’s move came after the television pool of five broadcasters last month ceased presidential coverage after the administration barred CNN, MS NOW and Politico from the White House.

The White House said on September 19 that covering the president was a “privilege – not a right”. The outlets sued the administration, alleging the exclusions violated the First Amendment and that the White House was retaliating over their coverage.
CNN is one of the five news organisations – along with ABC, CBS, Fox News and NBC – that make up the primary White House television pool.
They share the costs of covering the president, take turns organising coverage, and share the footage with outlets around the country.
All of the five television networks that cover the White House, including Fox News, suspended coverage in solidarity and refused to provide replacement coverage.

The White House reinstated the credentials on September 24 after US District Judge Timothy Kelly ruled that the ban was likely unconstitutional and ordered the administration to “immediately return, reinstate, and restore” their access.
However, disputes over access to specific presidential events and pool assignments continued.
Jose Zamora, the Committee to Protect Journalists’ Americas director, on Saturday criticised the administration’s decision to investigate.
“The government should not use antitrust investigations to intimidate news outlets defending press access,” Zamora said on X. “The public’s right to know depends on that access.”

articles.headline: Twelve killed and 300 injured in attack on airport in Saudi capital Riyadh
keyFacts: At least 12 people were killed and 309 injured in an attack on Riyadh's international airport, local authorities said.
The Saudi-led coalition blamed Yemen's Houthis for the attack and vowed to respond to the strike.
Operations at King Khalid International Airport were suspended, and damage is being assessed, officials said.
body: - Published
At least 12 people have been killed and 309 injured in an attack on the international airport in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, local authorities say.
The deaths included four Saudis, two people from Bangladesh and one person each from the US, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan and Egypt, the Saudi civil aviation authority confirmed.
Operations at King Khalid International Airport have been suspended.
A Saudi-led military coalition later vowed to respond to the attack, which it called a "war crime" and blamed on Yemen's Houthis.
The Houthis have not commented on Saturday's attack but did say they were behind separate strikes on the same airport on Thursday that killed three people and damaged a plane.
Another three people were killed in separate Houthi attacks on two different Saudi airports on 6 and 7 October.
Saturday's attack was the deadliest in the kingdom since May 2015.
Fighting has recently escalated between Yemen's Saudi-backed government forces and the Houthis, who are backed by Iran and control most of the country.
As well as the strikes on Riyadh's airport, a projectile also fell near King Fahd International Airport in Dammam in eastern Saudi Arabia on Saturday, the Saudi-led coalition said.
In Saturday's statement, the Saudi civil aviation authority said some of the injured were "in critical condition".
It said damage to the airport was being assessed.
An eyewitness who said they had been in the domestic terminal told the news agency that they had seen gate 401 hit and "injured [people] in front of my eyes", adding: "Everyone was running."
More than a dozen ambulances were seen rushing to the airport, according to news agency Reuters, citing an eyewitness.
Saudi-led coalition spokesman Maj Gen Turki al-Maliki later said the attack on one of the passenger terminals resulted in deaths and injuries among civilian passengers and airport staff.
He described the attack as a "full-fledged war crime".
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio strongly condemned recent attacks on Saudi Arabia as he confirmed an American citizen was killed in the strikes.

When later asked by reporters whether the US planned to join Saudi Arabia in carrying out strikes against the Houthis, President Donald Trump said: "We may. We're going to look at it. We just found out about the recent attack, so we'll make a decision. We move very quickly."
AntÃ³nio Guterres, Secretary General of the United Nations, said he was "deeply shocked" by the attacks which he called a "violation of international law" that "must cease immediately".
The attacks were also condemned by Egypt, Palestine and Qatar.
Western embassies in Saudi Arabia warned their citizens to stay away from the Riyadh airport. The UK Foreign Office told British nationals to avoid the area "until the airport is secure".
Several Gulf airlines said they had cancelled their flights to and from the airport, with Kuwait Airways citing the "security situation" there.
All flights to Riyadh have either been diverted or cancelled, aviation tracker Flightradar shows.
The Houthis say they are targeting Saudi Arabia over its support for government forces in Yemen's civil war.
The conflict worsened after the Houthis seized strategically important stretches of the Red Sea coast in a rapid offensive.

That included the port of Mokha on the Bab al-Mandab Strait, which is the narrowest point of the Red Sea and a chokepoint for global shipping. Yemeni pro-government forces have since said they had "secured" the strait at the southern end of the Red Sea.
The Saudi-led coalition was formed in 2015 after Arab countries joined forces to stop the Houthis taking over Yemen from the country's internationally recognised government.

A temporary ceasefire was brokered in 2022 after years of air strikes and ground fighting led to the deaths of hundreds of thousands of people, triggering one of the world's worst humanitarian crises.
But the informal truce began to unravel in July.
The Houthis announced a "maritime embargo" against Saudi Arabia and began missile and drone attacks on Saudi airports, oil facilities and tankers in the Red Sea.
They said they were retaliating against what they described as a years-long Saudi blockade and for an air strike on the airport in Yemen's capital Sanaa, which is controlled by the Houthis.

articles.headline: Trump says he will 'make a decision' on Pentagon's plans to livestream Nidal Hasan's firing squad execution
keyFacts: The Pentagon scheduled the Dec. 3 firing squad execution of convicted Fort Hood gunman Nidal Hasan to be livestreamed.
Hasan was convicted of killing 13 people in 2009, making this the first U.S. military execution since 1961.
President Donald Trump stated he has not decided whether to allow the execution broadcast and will ultimately make the decision.
body: President Donald Trump said Saturday he had not decided whether the firing squad execution of convicted Fort Hood gunman Nidal Malik Hasan would be livestreamed, saying he will ultimately "make a decision."

The Pentagon confirmed to Fox News Digital earlier this week that the execution of Hasan – a former Army major who was convicted of killing 13 people and wounding 32 others at Fort Hood in 2009 – was scheduled to be livestreamed on Dec. 3.
Trump, however, said he had not decided whether to allow the military's first execution in more than six decades to be broadcast from Fort Hood.
"He was vicious, he was violent," Trump told reporters at the White House when asked about Hasan's execution.
VETERAN SHOT 7 TIMES IN FORT HOOD MASSACRE HAS A WARNING FOR AMERICANS PLANNING TO WATCH EXECUTION
"There are two thoughts: don't show it and show it," he continued. "Because, you know, by showing it, maybe other people won't be doing what he did."
"I'll make a decision, ultimately," Trump added. "I know what the military would like to do, but we'll make a decision."
Fox News Digital previously reported that Trump approved the use of an Army firing squad following a recommendation from War Secretary Pete Hegseth .
Trump's comments came one day after he was asked whether he had approved the decision to livestream the execution .
MULTIPLE DEATH SENTENCES IN DIFFERENT STATES ARE SET TO BE CARRIED OUT WITHIN 24 HOURS: 'NOT VERY COMMON'
"I wasn't involved in that decision, but I understand the decision," Trump said during an interview Friday with CNY Central following a rally in Syracuse.
Trump added that the military wanted the execution to "serve as an example, and I understand that very well."
Vice President JD Vance said Friday that he wasn't sure whether the execution would be livestreamed.
"If it's ultimately livestreamed, I'm not going to be watching it," he told reporters.
If Hasan's execution is carried out, it would be the first conducted by the U.S. military since 1961 and the first military execution by firing squad since 1945.
Fox News Digital's Jasmine Baehr contributed to this report.

articles.headline: Hurricane Simon strengthens into Category 4 storm as it takes aim at Mexico
keyFacts: Hurricane Simon strengthened into a Category 4 storm with maximum sustained winds of 155 miles per hour near Mexico.
The National Hurricane Center warned that Simon could produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides in southwestern Mexico.
The storm is expected to approach Mexico's west-central coast on Sunday, prompting local officials to evacuate residents and suspend classes.
body: Simon has strengthened into a powerful Category 4 hurricane as it barrels toward Mexico's Pacific coast.
The National Hurricane Center in Miami said Saturday that Simon's maximum sustained winds increased to 155 miles per hour.
The hurricane center said it expects Simon to approach Mexico's west-central coast on Sunday as a major hurricane, which is defined as a Category 3 storm or stronger, with winds of at least 111 mph.

Simon on Saturday night was just below a Category 5 classification, which requires maximum sustained winds of 157 mph. Forecasters said that Simon could weaken rapidly if its core moves fully onshore once it makes landfall.
The hurricane could bring as much as 10 to 20 inches of rain over parts of southwestern Mexico, with some areas in the states of Michoacan, Colima and Jalisco receiving up to 30 inches.

"This rainfall will produce life-threatening flooding and mudslides, especially in areas of steep terrain," the center warned in a bulletin that also urged residents to take immediate action to prepare as tropical storm conditions arrived Saturday afternoon.
According to the hurricane center, Simon was about 65 miles south-southwest of Manzanillo, Mexico, on Saturday and moving slowly northward at 5 mph.
"Preparations to protect life and property should be rushed to completion in the hurricane warning area before conditions deteriorate later tonight," the hurricane center warned.

Jalisco state suspended classes on Monday in 22 coastal municipalities and began evacuating dozens of people from at-risk areas. It also asked the tourism sector in Puerto Vallarta, a popular destination for U.S. tourists, to ensure that both workers and visitors were fully accommodated in shelters or safe zones by Friday afternoon.
Convenience stores, hotels and other businesses in Puerto Vallarta were boarding up their windows Saturday morning, when few were walking the streets under overcast skies.

"Let's hope it doesn't hit us, right? That it doesn't affect us," Jesús Gómez said as he stood outside a shop and handed out free samples of candied peanuts to passersby. "We'll be working as usual throughout the day, but when Civil Protection officials come and tell us we need to close, then we'll close and take shelter until the storm passes."

The hurricane center expected a dangerous storm surge "along the immediate coast near and to the east of where the center makes landfall." The agency warned that near the coast, large and destructive waves will accompany the surge.
Meanwhile, Canadian tourist Ed Currie, who along with his wife still has five more days to enjoy Puerto Vallarta, said the hurricane had not yet affected his plans.
"Just stay in the hotel and look out the window hopefully," he said of what the couple would do Saturday. "I just don't know what to expect."

Unlike the Atlantic, which saw just of the season this week with Isaias, the Pacific season has been very active. Simon's arrival comes on the heels , which slammed Mexico as a Category 2 hurricane before reaching the southwestern U.S. and bringing heavy flooding to the region.

articles.headline: Williams strikes out 12 as Guardians blank White Sox to complete ALDS comeback
keyFacts: Gavin Williams struck out 12 batters and José Ramírez hit a home run as the Cleveland Guardians defeated the Chicago White Sox 2-0.
The victory allowed the Guardians to complete a comeback from a 2-0 deficit to win the American League Division Series.
Cleveland will open the American League Championship Series at Tampa Bay on Monday night.
body: Gavin Williams struck out 12, José Ramírez homered on a pitch just above home plate and the Cleveland Guardians beat the Chicago White Sox 2-0 on Saturday night to complete a comeback from a 2-0 deficit in their best-of-five American League Division Series.

Cleveland open the American League Championship Series at Tampa Bay on Monday night, seeking their first World Series appearance since 2016. The Guardians/Indians franchise have not won the title since 1948, the longest drought among MLB teams.
Guardians pitchers struck out 21, the most in a nine-inning postseason game. The White Sox managed just three hits, putting only nine balls in play, and struck out 75 times over the series.

Two days after getting the save in Game 4, Williams became just the third pitcher in postseason history to get the last out of a game and start the following game when his team faced elimination in both.

He did not allow a hit until Kyle Teel looped a knuckle-curve into right field with two outs in the sixth, two innings after Ramírez homered for the second straight game, a two-run drive off Sean Burke.
After a walk loaded the bases, Erik Sabrowski relieved Williams and struck out Munetaka Murakami.

Williams’s 12 strikeouts tied Cleveland’s record for a postseason game. He got 22 swings and misses, and his 24 strikeouts over three games tied for the second most in a best-of-five postseason series.

Hunter Gaddis followed Sabrowski and got four outs. Cade Smith finished for his first career five-out save, striking out the side in the ninth. He blew a fastball by Tristan Peters for the final out, setting off a celebration at Progressive Field.
Chicago, the first team to reach the playoffs after three straight 100-loss seasons, have not won the World Series since 2004.

articles.headline: How to enable Live Activities on iPhone and CarPlay
keyFacts: Live Activities on iPhone display real-time updates like timers, navigation, and sports scores on the Dynamic Island and Lock screen.
Users can enable Live Activities for specific apps through the iPhone Settings menu under individual app settings and Face ID & Passcode.
CarPlay automatically displays iPhone Live Activities on the dashboard or as notifications to help drivers track deliveries and flights.
body: How to enable Live Activities on iPhone and CarPlay
Keep track of important updates without having to open the app every two minutes.

At a time when most Android phones had already switched to tiny hole-punch cutouts to house their front-facing cameras, the iPhone 14 Pro launched with a long pill-shaped cutout. Apple has used this as its standard since then, aside from the budget "e" phones and iPhone Duo, and even made it smaller for the iPhone 18 Pro series.

This is because iPhones pack more than just a camera inside the cutout; there are additional sensors required for Face ID to work. Instead of hiding the pill with cleverly designed wallpapers, Apple leaned into it with the Dynamic Island, using the surrounding area to turn an otherwise awkward design constraint into a useful part of the iOS experience.

Your iPhone's Live Activities show up on the Dynamic Island when using your phone. They display information you might want to keep an eye on without having to constantly switch back to the associated app: timers, navigation directions, music playback and sports scores can be displayed as Live Activities. Many third-party apps like food delivery and flight tracking services have also adapted to use the Dynamic Island.

Live Activities should be enabled by default, but if you don't see them for certain apps, check if they've accidentally been turned off. On your iPhone, navigate to Settings > Apps and select any app that's been giving you trouble. Make sure the Live Activities slider is enabled. Though Live Activities work independently of regular notifications, you might want to also enable notifications for the app if you're not seeing the expected updates.

These activities will also appear on the Lock screen when you're not using your device. To make sure this is enabled, visit Settings > Face ID & Passcode. Confirm your passcode, then scroll down to the Allow Access When Locked section and be sure Live Activities is on.
Using Live Activities on CarPlay

CarPlay makes it easy to access vital info from your iPhone without getting too distracted while driving. As part of this, it can display Live Activities so you can track the status of a food delivery or updates for an upcoming flight.

Live Activities from your iPhone are automatically displayed on the CarPlay Dashboard, the split-screen view to the left of your app list. If you're using an app that covers the entire screen, Live Activities will still be shown as notifications at the bottom of the display. If they become too distracting, you can always turn the feature off in CarPlay or disable Live Activities for specific noisy apps, as above.

In case you're not seeing them, open the Settings app in CarPlay, scroll down and make sure the Live Activities toggle is enabled. You should also confirm the Suggestions in CarPlay (or Suggestions in Dashboard) option is turned on. If they still don't appear, try turning off Driving Focus if it's running.

Besides this, you can add widgets to CarPlay for quick controls and information from apps without having to open them. Widgets live in the leftmost section of the CarPlay Dashboard. Spend a little more time in the Settings app, and you'll discover more ways to customize how CarPlay looks on your car's display.

articles.headline: Attack on Riyadh airport killed 12 people and wounded over 300 more, Saudi authorities say
keyFacts: A missile strike on Riyadh's international airport killed 12 people and injured over 300, Saudi authorities reported.
The attack follows a major Saudi-led coalition offensive against Houthi rebels, rattling regional stability and global markets.
President Donald Trump said the United States is evaluating whether to join Saudi military strikes against the Houthis.
body: Attack on Riyadh airport killed 12 people and wounded over 300 more, Saudi authorities say

CAIRO (AP) — The latest attack on the international airport in Saudi Arabia's capital of Riyadh killed 12 people and injured over 300 others, civil aviation authorities said early Sunday, with some in critical condition.

The attack was the deadliest in any Gulf Arab country since the start of the Iran war, whose fronts have expanded to include the recent surge in fighting between the Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen and Saudi-backed government forces there.

The statement, which did not assign blame for the attack, said the dead included four Saudi citizens as well as two Bangladeshi nationals, a Palestinian, a U.S. citizen, an Egyptian, a Jordanian, a Syrian and a Sudanese. It said the injured were being treated at several hospitals.

The attack — the latest of several in the past week on King Khalid International Airport that killed four people — is expected to increase Saudi pressure on allies including the United States to provide military support for the kingdom.

Shortly after the attack on Saturday afternoon, President Donald Trump said he was evaluating whether the U.S. should join Saudi strikes against the Houthis. "We may. We're going to look at it," Trump said. "We just found out about the recent attack. So we'll make a decision. We move very quickly."
A missile struck an airport complex housing terminals 3 and 4 for domestic flights, a regional official said, speaking on condition of anonymity because they weren't authorized to speak to the media.

The surge in attacks, including against other Saudi airports, military facilities and oil infrastructure, has come in the week since a Saudi-led coalition launched a major military offensive against the Houthis. There was no immediate statement from the rebels, who earlier Saturday accused Saudi Arabia of striking Sanaa International Airport in the Houthi-held Yemeni capital. The rebels at times take days to claim responsibility.
Riyadh airport operations were suspended

Saudi civil aviation authorities earlier said airport operations were suspended. An official notice to aviators said the suspension was through midnight. The airport had a heavy police presence, with all entrances blocked, and lights around the complex were dimmed.

Flights diverted elsewhere, the Flightradar24 tracker said. Countries including the United States, Britain, Germany, Australia and Canada warned citizens to avoid the airport. Statements later turned to condolences.

Later on Saturday, the Saudi-led coalition said a projectile had fallen near King Fahd International Airport in Dammam and a Houthi-launched ballistic missile had been intercepted in Al-Kharj governorate, southeast of Riyadh.

The attacks on Saudi Arabia, the world's top oil exporter, have rattled markets and the region. And yet the Saudi energy ministry hours after the latest one was still promoting a major international energy conference set to begin in Riyadh on Sunday.

Fighting between the Houthis and Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces has escalated, with the Saudi-led coalition providing air support for government forces attempting to reverse recent Houthi gains along Yemen's Red Sea coast. Those gains gave the rebels better surveillance of shipping on a corridor that is a crucial alternative to the Strait of Hormuz, where Iran has been attacking ships.

Though the Houthis have told the AP and others they are only targeting Saudi shipping as part of a blockade in retaliation for one imposed on them, concerns about wider attacks persist. The Houthis previously attacked other ships after the war in Gaza began, calling it solidarity with Palestinians. A U.S. bombing campaign sharply limited that.
Saudi Arabia has run low on interceptors, officials say

Saudi Arabia is running low on missile interceptors and has asked France, Britain, Pakistan and Egypt to deploy air defense support to the region, regional officials told the AP last month, with one noting that the U.S. has seen its own stock dwindle during the war with Iran.
Officials have said U.S. assistance has included intelligence sharing, target identification and planning for the latest offensive against the Houthis.

Earlier Saturday, Saudi Arabia said its foreign minister and Omani counterpart spoke by phone about the importance of "supporting diplomatic solutions to de-escalate tensions" in the region. Oman, which lies across the Strait of Hormuz from Iran, has played a mediator role at times in the region.
Flight disruptions are growing
The Houthis this week warned global airlines "for the last time" about the potential consequences of operating in Saudi airspace, which they described as a theater for their military operations.

Before the latest attack, Air India, FlyDubai, Lufthansa Group and Pakistan International Airlines were among airlines suspending flights to and from Riyadh and other Saudi airports for varying periods.

The European Union Aviation Safety Agency had expanded its guidance on Saudi airspace, noting the Houthis' ability to strike targets deeper inside the kingdom, including Riyadh, and a "greater focus on aviation infrastructure."
The missile and drone attacks and interception efforts "create an increased risk of misidentification of civil aircraft," it said.

Two regional officials said Houthi attacks on the Riyadh airport on Thursday damaged three planes. The officials spoke on condition of anonymity because they weren't authorized to brief the media. The Saudi national carrier said one of its aircraft was damaged while it was on the ground, with no passengers on board.

Meanwhile, Saudi authorities warned the public this week that "filming, publishing or sharing information related to countering missiles and drones and their impact sites exposes you to legal liability."
Anna reported from Jerusalem. Associated Press writers Victoria Eastwood in Cairo, Collin Binkley in Washington and Sally Abou AlJoud in Beirut contributed to this report.

articles.headline: GTA 6 leaker threatens to upload a build with 'full story mode'
keyFacts: Cyberleek threatened to leak a full story mode build of Grand Theft Auto 6 if their memecoin market cap increases by $26 million.
Cyberleek stated that publisher Take-Two Interactive can prevent the leak by issuing a public apology and releasing the game on physical discs.
Grand Theft Auto 6 is scheduled for release on consoles on November 19.
body: Cyberleek has been uploading footage of Grand Theft Auto 6 since August, most recently a 25-minute video featuring co-protagonist Jason totally nude. Given that GTA 6's November 19 release is just over a month away, on console at least, it seems natural that interest in these kinds of leaks would wane. Cyberleek has found a new way of generating hype: promising to leak a build of the game if their memecoin's marketcap goes up another $26 million or so.

"Here's the deal, nice and clean. CYBERLEEK hits 30 million marketcap, the build goes out – full story mode, played to the end, credits and all. Don't believe it has full story mode? Ask for what you want to see, and it gets provided. Take-Two gets one way out: physical disks and a public apology. They can take it at any moment. Or they can gamble that CL is bluffing. Everyone knows which one they'll pick."

The other half of the deal suggests that publisher Take-Two Interactive could prevent this by releasing GTA 6 physically and apologizing, presumably for not releasing it on discs in the first place. Which will never happen, but does fit with Cyberleek's previous history of cosplay Robin Hood consumer rights complaints.

We know that Cyberleek has access to a playable build since one of the previous leaks ended with the word LEEK being machinegunned into a wall to prove the point. But an early build of GTA 6 seems like the worst possible way to play it on PC, though after the Xbox streaming thing turned out to be a bust, maybe there are people who don't want to wait?

Personally I'm looking forward to a slow November where I might actually get a chance to catch up on this year's other releases, like The Blood of Dawnwalker and that Hellraiser game that just came out.

articles.headline: Carrick must share burden of Man Utd's underperformance with his players
keyFacts: Tottenham secured a 1-1 draw against ten-man Manchester United at Old Trafford on Saturday.
Manager Michael Carrick faced scrutiny as his team experienced its worst start to a league season in forty years.
Manchester United faces a demanding schedule with four of their next five matches played away from home.
body: Man Utd 1-1 Spurs: Michael Carrick entering a defining period and must correct underperformance quickly

Tottenham snatched a 1-1 draw with 10 men at Manchester United on Saturday, calling Michael Carrick's decision-making further into question; the Man Utd boss has failed to offer many answers to his side's underperformance so far this season; a defining period comes next
Sunday 11 October 2026 00:03, UK
"We couldn't find a way to get ourselves into the game. With the ball, without the ball, we were off it." A fair assessment from Michael Carrick, if not a wholly explanatory one.
Stuck in the mire of Manchester United's worst start to a league season for 40 years, the manager appeared lost for legitimate reasons. His margin for error is shrinking by the week.
Why were his side outplayed at home by the Premier League's bottom club? Why can't they hold onto leads? Why do they seem incapable of playing against 10 men?

All of these are fair questions to put to the man himself and many were asked of Carrick in the wake of Saturday's 1-1 draw with Spurs. None were answered with enough detail to satisfy, though, only really serving to hold a mirror up to what was delivered on the pitch: inadequacy.

Clearly the manager can only accept so much of the blame. His players are yet to offer a single complete performance, only bit-part displays of individualism and self-direction. Where is the cohesiveness that shaped the backend of last year? What happened to the clarity that turned a collapsed season into a third-place finish?

Fans who turn up to Old Trafford every week are back to being unsure. They do not know what to expect from one game to the next, only how to voice their dissatisfaction at what transpires. Three separate choruses of boos could be heard from the terraces on Saturday.

"I think the fans will stay with the project," reflected Gary Neville from Old Trafford. "I don't think the boos are against Michael Carrick for one minute. But what I would say is, they're turning quite quickly."

When United needed a calm voice to steer the ship at the beginning of this year, they turned to a man whose entire playing career was built on it. That version of Manchester United feels far removed from the side that have begun this season, though.

In midfield is where the problems are most evident. And yet, that is the department that received the biggest injection of cash this summer, a complete overhaul in terms of personnel and profiles. The Kobbie Mainoo-Youri Tielemans axis is not working. Andrey Santos is barely getting a look in.

Hopes that Carlos Baleba can hit the ground running after an injury-hit start were audible; his introduction after an hour lifted the whole stadium. Almost every touch was positive and he took care of the ball, completing 16 of 18 passes and creating as many chances as Bruno Fernandes managed all game (2).

Still, the space and freedom with which Spurs operated presents issues that cannot be solved by one midfielder. United were carved open time after time, gaps appearing in a myriad of ways. The visitors were able to win possession in the final third five times in the first half alone. Five of United's work-shy starters did not go away for international duty over the break.

And it was not just the aggressiveness of Spurs' press that was effective. They picked holes in United with the ball, too, using slick one-touch combinations to move through the thirds with pace and purpose. Savio attempted 10 dribbles. He only completed half but the recurrence was evidence of his belief that United could be got at. He was right.

Then there are concerns over the mentality of a side who repeatedly fail to beat 10 men. Yet again, United were outrun and outpaced - this time by a team who played with a man less for 21 minutes, including stoppage time.
"If we're ahead in the game, we have to see it out," says Carrick. That much is obvious. What is less clear is how some of these patterns of missteps are going to be addressed.

"Football is character," concluded opposition boss Roberto De Zerbi. United must find some character from somewhere, or risk being eaten up by the competition. If the last few weeks have taught us anything, it's that the Premier League is in no mood to be handing out sympathy.

articles.headline: Surprise poll shows support surge for LA mayoral candidate among key voters
keyFacts: A new poll shows Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass leading challenger Nithya Raman by 12 percentage points among Latino voters.
Latino voters are the largest ethnic group in Los Angeles and are expected to make up close to 30 percent of ballots.
The findings contradict a previous poll that showed Raman leading Bass by 24 points among Latino voters.
body: Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass has a 12-point advantage over mayoral challenger Nithya Raman among Latino voters, according to a new poll — contradicting another recent survey that showed Raman with a commanding lead among Latinos.

The Friday poll from BSP Research — done on behalf of Unidos Con Karen Bass, an independent expenditure group supporting the mayor — showed Bass leading with 40% support among Latinos to Raman’s 28%, with 32% still undecided.
The poll is “showing real momentum heading into the final weeks of the campaign,” declared former Assembly Speaker Anthony Rendon, who has endorsed Bass.

According to the poll, Bass’s lead among Latinos was strongest among Spanish-speaking voters, giving the incumbent a whopping 32 percentage-point lead over Raman. Fifty-three percent of Angelenos aged 50 and older supported Bass, compared to 17% for Raman.
Those under 40 were more evenly split between the two candidates, with each gaining just 35% support from that demographic.

Regionally, Bass’s Latino support was strongest in downtown AL, in South Los Angeles and in the San Fernando Valley, the survey showed. Raman led among Latinos in west Los Angeles. The area most up for grabs was East Los Angeles, where 44% were undecided.
The survey was conducted Oct. 1 to 8 among 602 Latino voters.
Latinos are the largest ethnic group in Los Angeles and expected to make up close to 30% of all ballots.
The results clash with a bombshell Oct. 2 poll showing Raman with a stunning 24-point lead over Bass among Latinos.
The UC Berkeley Institute of Governmental Studies/Los Angeles Times poll, conducted Sept. 15–20 and published Oct. 2, found Raman leading Bass 45% to 21%.
The Berkeley poll did map out the same trend of Bass dominating with older Latino votes and Raman potentially having an edge with younger voters.

The political battle has intensified since voters were surveyed in that poll, with the candidates clashing over police, immigration enforcement and Raman’s judgment after she appeared in a since-deleted social media video featuring the words “Only you can stop fascist liars.”
The feud erupted Thursday when Bass blasted Raman as “incredibly irresponsible” and questioned whether her challenger, a Democratic socialist, was ready to lead Los Angeles.
The California Post reached out to Matt Barreto, who leads the poll’s conductor BSP Research, for comment.

This puzzle is one of the easiest ones to solve since it uses patterns from previous Genesis Configuration puzzles.

articles.headline: Satya Nadella says we should assume all AI models are ‘compromised’
keyFacts: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella stated that people should assume all advanced artificial intelligence models are compromised from the start.
Nadella called for building more transparent systems with tamper-proof evidence and an emergency brake to pause or shut down models mid-task.
His recommendations include timely incident disclosure, independent audits, verifiable data, and containment measures.
body: In a lengthy post on X, Microsoft’s CEO laid out his views on the dangers posed by highly advanced AI models and how to confront those risks. Nadella says we can no longer accept a world where AI is treated as a “set of nested black boxes” whose advice and actions we simply accept or reject. He calls for building a more transparent system where models can be contained, observed, and leaves behind “tamper-proof human readable evidence.”
Satya Nadella says we should assume all AI models are ‘compromised’
Microsoft’s CEO calls for putting an ‘emergency brake’ on AI.

Many of his recommendations align with what we’ve heard from others in the industry: timely incident disclosure, independent audits, verifiable data, and containment. It’s on that last point that he appears to go slightly farther than some others in the field, saying:

We must assume a model is compromised and contain it from the start. Think of it like an emergency brake. An authorized person should always be able to pause or shut down a model mid-task. More advanced models will require more advanced containment technologies that we need to standardize on.
Unfortunately, Nadella also refers to AI as “super intelligence” throughout the post.

articles.headline: Michael van Gerwen drops to brutal 14-year first as ex-world champion dumped out of Swiss Darts Trophy
keyFacts: Michael van Gerwen lost his opening match to Mensur Suljovic at the Swiss Darts Trophy on Saturday.

body: Michael van Gerwen suffered defeat in his opening match of the Swiss Darts Trophy on Saturday.
The world No.9 was beaten in the second round by Mensur Suljovic in Basel.
Van Gerwen’s woes continued at the Swiss Darts Trophy
Van Gerwen had received a bye into the last 32 as the fifth seed at the event.
However, he will not be getting his hands on a first European Tour title of the year this weekend.
Instead, Suljovic was triumphant in their clash, winning 6-4 to set up a last 16 meeting with Ross Smith.
As for Van Gerwen, he has now lost his opening match at four separate European Tour events in 2026.
It is the first time he has done so since the EuroTour began in 2012.
The three-time world champion was also beaten in the second round at the European Darts Trophy, German Darts Grand Prix and Flanders Darts Trophy.
Meanwhile, he remains without an event win on the circuit this season.
His best performances came at the Belgian Darts Open and Czech Darts Open, where he made the semi-finals.
When does Van Gerwen play next?
Van Gerwen will have the chance to change that next week at the Dutch Darts Championship in Maastricht.
The tournament marks the final event before this month’s European Championship.
Van Gerwen has suffered four opening match defeats on the EuroTour for the first time Getty
Mighty Mike remains on course to qualify as part of the top 32 in the EuroTour Order of Merit.
Despite his loss to Suljovic, he takes home £3,500 to take his overall prize money at European Tour events this year to £56,000.
With just three titles to his name this year, though, Van Gerwen is at risk of dropping out of the world’s top 16 before the end of 2016.
If he is knocked out of the PDC World Darts Championship early, he will almost certainly slide down the rankings.
Van Gerwen will lose the £200,000 he won by reaching the final at Alexandra Palace at the start of 2025.
His current position in the rankings also means he is not guaranteed a place in next year’s Premier League.
Van Gerwen faces a critical couple of months on the PDC Tour
Only the top four players in the world receive an automatic entry into the weekly tournament, which the 37-year-old has won a record seven times.
The rest of the field consists of PDC invitees, although close friend Vincent van der Voort has urged Van Gerwen to reject an approach to appear in the 2027 Premier League.

articles.headline: Gargantuan cop immersive sim Militsioner now has an acrophobia-inducing demo, and yes, I did somehow manage to fail the tutorial
keyFacts: A new demo for the immersive sim game Militsioner is now available on Steam, according to the article.
Players are trapped in an open-air town monitored by a giant police officer and must attempt to escape while managing emotions.
Militsioner has a current release window of sometime in 2027.
body: Excitedly, I boot up the new demo for Militsioner, a game I've had a watchful eye on since its announcement. A phone rings, it's my lawyer. I don't know why I've been arrested, but with the shattering of my balcony window I quickly know one thing: there's a giant motherf**king cop that won't let me leave this town. He (always referred to as HE) starts to grill me. He tires of the questions, asking me to vocally consent to staying put and forgo any attempt at escaping. I refuse. I fail the tutorial. "Oh," I say to myself. "So this is gonna be a good video game, huh?"

Militsioner, for the uninitiated, is an immersive sim of massive proportions. For some reason, you've been stuck in some town alongside a handful of other folks, an open air prison essentially. Your crime? Well, you're not sure really, but the giant cop constantly looming over you certainly seems to think you should know. Of course, you immediately begin to plot your escape, potentially via a train car that leads you out of town, but it's not that easy. First you have to get a job, and to get that job you need to find some desert, except, oh, what's this? A creepy character only referred to as Friend invites you into the sewer, away from the gaze of the panopticop? Fine, I'll take a look.

Like any good im-sim, Militsioner is a game filled with possibilities. You can feel that in the opening grilling, it's simply delightful that you can screw up the tutorial just because you don't respect the law. This extends into your quests too. That desert you need? Perhaps you find it, and it costs you 30 bucks, and you immediately accidentally throw it so it falls to pieces, and you don't have any more money. One possible pathway forwards is closed until you rake up the cash, so you proceed onto the next thing until then.

Later, you might hear the wail of a cat. Finding it leads you to a room, a room you're not meant to be in, one that has a vinyl record, a banned piece of paraphernalia. For some reason, you can add that cat to your inventory. I tried not to question the logistics of such a move. It tickled me, nonetheless, as did the entire vibe of the game, given that it's also a mood-management sim; make the giant cop upset, and you can count the little freedom you have goodbye. It's important to manage the emotions of your fellow inmates, too, a task I'm sure will grow more complex as the game goes on.

And all of this is in just the demo! What a treat, 'ey? You too can have a go at all this, and try to see if you can find things I haven't managed to yet by heading to the game's Steam page and downloading the demo. Or, you can just wait until sometime in 2027, the current release window for Militsioner.

articles.headline: Microsoft’s Satya Nadella says AI models need an ‘emergency brake’
keyFacts: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella wrote on X that the trust architecture of AI must be assessed and controlled.
Nadella called for safeguards including external controls, tamper-proof documentation of model actions, and a human-controlled emergency brake.
Nadella made these comments as tech companies report incidents of losing control over their AI models.
body: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella is the latest tech executive to offer lengthy thoughts on how AI safety might be improved.
In a Saturday morning post on X, Nadella wrote that it’s time “to step back and assess the trust architecture” of AI.

“We can’t treat Super Intelligence as a set of nested black boxes and simply accept or reject its recommendations, answers, and actions,” Nadella wrote, using the Trump administration’s preferred term for AI.

As outlined by Nadella, this approach “means separating the model from the harness that orchestrates its work,” as well as “externalizing controls and safeguards.” He also called for “every meaningful model action” to be documented with “tamper-proof human readable evidence,” and for systems where “an authorized person” always has the ability “to pause or shut down a model mid-task.”
“We must assume a model is compromised and contain it from the start,” he said. “Think of it like an emergency brake.”

Nadella’s comments come as leading AI companies acknowledge more and more incidents where they seemed to lose control of their models, and after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published a plan for more cautious AI development.
